title: Your first safari: what to expect and what to pack
excerpt: Early starts, open vehicles and a lot of wonder. A simple, honest guide for first-time safari travellers.

body.p: A first safari can feel like a step into the unknown. It needn't. Here is what a typical day looks like, what to bring and how to get the most from every drive.

ul: A wake-up call before sunrise, with coffee and something light
A morning game drive of three to four hours, when animals are most active
Brunch back at the lodge, then free time through the heat of the day
An afternoon drive into the evening, often with a sundowner stop
Dinner together, and stories from the day

body.p: Most drives are in open vehicles with an experienced guide, and sometimes a tracker. Stay seated, keep your voice low and your arms inside the vehicle, and always follow your guide's instructions. Wild animals are used to vehicles, not to people stepping out of them.
Every drive is different. Some mornings bring a leopard in a tree; others are about the small things: a dung beetle, a weaver's nest, a sunrise. That is part of the magic.

ul: Neutral colours (khaki, olive, beige) in layers, as mornings and evenings can be cold
A warm fleece or jacket, a sun hat, sunglasses and sunscreen
Binoculars and a camera with a zoom lens
A soft bag rather than a hard suitcase if you are flying between camps
Any personal medication, plus copies of your passport and insurance

body.p: Some safari areas are in malaria zones and some, such as Pilanesberg and the reserves near Cape Town, are malaria-free. Speak to a travel doctor about vaccinations and malaria precautions well before you travel, and make sure your travel insurance covers your whole trip.
Tipping guides, trackers and lodge staff is customary across Africa and greatly appreciated. We'll give you guidance on amounts for each lodge before you go.
